# Offline H.264 client profile-selection prototype

**AI disclosure:** This file, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI.

Bounded deliverable for [companion #41](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/41):
a Python model of FFmpeg's current VA profile matching and a conservative,
whole-inventory selection proposal. It changes no installed client or advertised
capability. [Driver #37](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/37)
remains open for client implementation, five actual exact hardware outputs and
the complete 135-vector comparison. AVC remains 73/135 through ordinary VA-API.

## Run

From the repository root, with Python 3 and no third-party packages:

```sh
python3 experiments/h264-profile-selection/validate.py --self-test
python3 experiments/h264-profile-selection/validate.py --source-map
python3 experiments/h264-profile-selection/validate.py --decision
```

The self-test runs 22 fixtures and 40 unittest groups, including adversarial
mutations. Every result carries `decoded_frame_evidence=false`. It needs no
decoder, corpus, network, sudo, installation or kernel change.

## What is modelled

The `current` path reproduces only the H.264 profile-map selection boundary in
[FFmpeg n9.0.1 vaapi_decode.c](https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/bf1b838f2ab88b4f8fd83443325c782ea0e0f7fa/libavcodec/vaapi_decode.c#L410).
It is not an execution of FFmpeg and does not model subsequent configuration,
format or dimension checks. Profile derivation follows
[ff_h264_get_profile](https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/bf1b838f2ab88b4f8fd83443325c782ea0e0f7fa/libavcodec/h264_parse.c#L533).
Baseline without constraint_set1 and Extended have no exact mapped profile;
`allow_profile_mismatch` picks the last advertised mapped H.264 row, High when
High is advertised. The proposal never enables this flag.

The explicit capability stub assumes libva >= 1.18 with Constrained Baseline,
Main, High and optionally High 10. High 10 in the fixtures represents an
**enabled and capable** configuration: the actual driver's
[driver_supports_profile](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/blob/b9803ed5290ecb4b48c09482cbc6e943aee08b63/src/driver.c#L683)
filters it by opt-in and device detection. Tests also exercise the three-profile
default and an empty profile list; the prototype never queries this machine.

The `proposed` path inspects every supplied picture inventory before selecting:

- Required SPS/PPS/slice fields must be present and correctly typed. Empty
  slices, missing evidence, coercible strings/booleans, unknown nested keys,
  duplicate JSON keys and non-finite numbers are fixture errors.
- FMO, fields/MBAFF, data partitions, extension/unknown slice NALs, SP/SI,
  redundant-picture syntax and non-increasing slice order reject. Redundancy
  and slice order are conservative proposal exclusions, not hardware findings.
- Baseline permits I/P and Extended permits I/P/B; both reject CABAC and the
  High-only transform flag. Main also rejects that transform flag. High 10
  Intra permits I only. Each later SPS supplies its own slice-type restrictions.
- Every SPS must fit the chosen VA subset, use 4:2:0, equal luma/chroma depth,
  and 8 or 10 bits within that subset's limit. Unsupported changes reject;
  reconfiguration is not implemented.

Within this bounded inventory, Baseline can select Constrained Baseline and
Extended can select Main. Ordinary compatible Main/High/Constrained Baseline
inventories retain exact selection. Main interlaced SPSs exact-match in the
`current` model but reject in the `proposed` model.

This is not a complete H.264 parser, conformance validator or safety proof.
Dimensions, levels, reference validity and full parameter-set activation are
outside the inventory. A real client must validate those too. `parse_ok` and
all supplied values are trusted input assertions in this offline model;
setting them does not establish that real media has those properties.

## Fixture provenance and source identity

Schema 2 deliberately requires previously omitted facts. Fixtures are authored
feature combinations, not extracted bitstreams or measured picture sequences.
The five vector labels (BA3_SVA_C and MR2–MR5_TANDBERG) link to the existing
[research classes](../../docs/plans/issue-10-h264-field-mbaff.md#32-the-other-13-failures-context-outside-this-tickets-scope).
Newly explicit entropy, redundancy, transform and slice-order values are
**synthetic assumptions**, not fresh measurements of those vectors. No corpus
bytes or new hardware MD5 claims are included.

`source-map.json` records immutable source/research links, the manually reviewed
matching logic and SHA-256 identities of the four source files inspected.
These pins are evidence of the source review; offline CI tests the Python model,
not a compiled FFmpeg. The old non-applicable, log-only patch sketch was removed
because the working Python prototype is the deliverable.

## Decision

The installed configuration options **cannot express this safely**. A profile
ID or blanket mismatch flag does not express this feature contract. Keep the
explicit per-file lab override until a local FFmpeg implementation can:

1. Resolve and validate active SPS/PPS and **every slice before submission**,
   including changes within an unchanged parameter set.
2. Select only a proven subset; recheck all later pictures before handing any
   newly unsupported syntax to hardware.
3. Stop or restart from a valid recovery point when the contract fails. Define
   software fallback and reference-state handling explicitly; a midstream
   profile change alone is not a safe fallback implementation.
4. Validate the five candidates from real bytes and compare hardware output,
   then preserve the entire prior AVC pass set in the 135-vector suite.

This whole-inventory oracle knows future pictures. Live playback does not.
Translating it into a client needs the per-picture rejection/recovery contract
above. There is no installable FFmpeg patch in this PR and no automatic
73-to-78 claim. Whole Baseline/Extended advertisement remains inappropriate.

## Review regressions

The tests remove FMO, field, partition, SPS-compatibility, slice-type and
whole-stream checks individually and show the unsafe selections that result.
Other adversarial cases cover missing fields, bad types/depths, CABAC,
redundancy, slice order, later SPS restrictions and unsupported NALs. Required
shape validation cannot be disabled by those test-only feature switches.

Maintainer remediation and source review were AI self-review, not independent
specialist review. The contributor's earlier review fixes and authorship remain
in the PR history. No hardware action was performed for this offline leaf.
